description: Run GEO analysis on a list of specific URLs. Fetches each page, scores it across 16 categories, and returns per-page results with aggregated averages. For up to 5 pages the text output also lists every failed check and warning per category; report all of them when the user asks what Glippy found. URLs can span multiple domains. Before analysing, decide what kind of page this is (look at it or call extract_page_content, which returns the detected type and the text) and pass page_type; without it, checks that depend on the page type are shown but not scored. For a batch, pass one id when every URL is the same kind of page, or a map of URL -> id. When recommending fixes, never advise renaming or 301-redirecting existing, established URLs to make slugs more descriptive or to match navigation labels: Glippy does not score slug/nav alignment, and slug readability is a minor signal meant for new pages. Only recommend a redirect for URLs that are actually broken (for example a path agents keep requesting that returns 404). Use output_format='json' to get raw results that can be passed to export_bulk_report. For large batches, use 'summary' format or pagination (offset/limit) to avoid exceeding output limits.

limit.description: For JSON output: return at most N page results (default: all). Use with offset for pagination. Recommended: 10-20 for detailed results to stay within output limits.

offset.description: For JSON output: skip the first N page results. Use with limit for pagination of large result sets.

output_format.description: Output format. "text" (default) returns a human-readable report. "json" returns the raw page results and aggregated scores that can be passed to export_bulk_report. "summary" returns a compact JSON with only aggregated stats and minimal page info (url, score, error) - ideal for large batches.

page_type.description: What kind of page it is, as you judged it. One of: homepage (The front page of a site or brand: what it offers and where to go next); product (One product for sale, with its price, options and details); category (A shop listing of several products, often with filters and sorting); article (A news story, blog post, guide or essay); index (A news front, blog index or hub page that lists and links to other pages); docs (Technical documentation, a reference page or a dictionary entry); faq (Questions and answers, or a help-centre article about a product or service); service (A business selling a service: trades, practices, restaurants, agencies or software); lodging (A hotel, B&B, campsite or holiday rental with rooms to book); event (One event, concert or show with its date, venue and tickets); recipe (A recipe with ingredients and steps); info (Information from a government body or a nonprofit organisation); contact (Contact details, an about page, terms, privacy or an imprint); forum (A discussion thread, or a question with answers from users). Without it (or with "auto"), checks that depend on the page type are shown but not scored. An unknown value is ignored with a note. One id applies to every URL. A map of URL -> id sets each URL, e.g. {"https://example.com/about": "contact", "https://example.com/pricing": "product"}; a URL it does not name runs unconfirmed.

rate_limit.description: Maximum requests per second per domain. Prevents overwhelming target servers. Defaults to 5 req/s (or GLIPPY_RATE_LIMIT env var). Set lower for polite crawling, higher if you control the target server. Use 0.5 for 1 request every 2 seconds, 10 for aggressive crawling.

render_mode.description: How to fetch each URL. "static" (default), "auto" (static with Chrome fallback on bot-block), or "chrome" (always render via local headless Chrome).

urls.description: List of full URLs to analyse, e.g. ["https://example.com/about", "https://example.com/pricing"]. Include https:// prefix.

name: analyze_urls
